plan_needed: A Claude account. Anthropic's Slack page names Team and Enterprise, and its blog says Pro and Max were added on 26 January 2026; Free isn't mentioned. Slack's docs say your Slack workspace admin must approve the MCP integration. On Claude Team or Enterprise an Owner adds the connector first (see claude-owner-adds-slack).

steps.where: Claude (claude.ai or the desktop app), Customize
steps.do: Go to Customize > Connectors and select Discover.
steps.see: The Connectors directory opens.

steps.do: Search for Slack (made by Slack, Anthropic verified) and open its page. Select Connect to Claude. On Team or Enterprise, an Owner sees Connect for your team instead.
steps.see: You're sent to Slack to sign in.

steps.do: Sign in to your Slack workspace, review the access Claude asks for and approve it.
steps.see: The exact Slack approval screen isn't described in the docs we read. Slack's docs say the integration must be approved by your Slack workspace admin.

steps.do: Check the connector list.
steps.see: Slack shows under Your connectors with the status Connected.

steps.do: Select + in the message box, then Connectors, and switch Slack on.
steps.see: Claude can search channels you can access, read threads and canvases, and send messages. It can ask before using a tool, depending on your tool permissions.

steps.do: Ask something like "What did the team decide about the launch date in #product-planning last week?"
steps.see: Claude searches your channels, DMs and files and answers from what it finds.

undo.do: Select Slack under Your connectors and select Disconnect. To take it off your account, open the three-dot menu and select Remove.
undo.see: Claude is signed out of Slack. The Slack-side steps aren't described in the docs we read.

plan_needed: Claude Team or Enterprise, Owner role. Slack Enterprise+ organisations on Claude Team or Enterprise can also manage access through Okta.

steps.do: Go to Organization settings > Connectors and click Browse connectors.
steps.see: The list of available connectors.

steps.do: Select Slack and click Add to your team.
steps.see: Slack becomes available to the organisation. Nobody gets access automatically; each person still signs in.

steps.do: Optionally set each Slack tool or group of tools to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked. Consider Needs approval for sending messages and editing canvases.
steps.see: The settings apply across the organisation and members can't override them.

steps.do: Each person follows claude-to-slack and signs in to Slack themselves.
steps.see: Each person sees only what their own Slack account can see.

undo.do: Remove the Slack connector for the organisation.
undo.see: Members can no longer use it. The exact button for removal at organisation level isn't named in the docs we read.

plan_needed: Claude Team or Enterprise (public beta), run by an Owner of the Claude organisation, with a Slack workspace admin to install the app and run the pairing command. Not available on Free, Pro or Max, or with Zero Data Retention, customer-managed encryption or the HIPAA configuration. Routines must be enabled. Team plans need usage credits loaded.

steps.do: Click Start setup (or Resume setup).
steps.see: The setup page walks through pairing, optional GitHub and credits, then launch.

steps.where: Claude Tag setup page, then the Slack Marketplace
steps.do: Click Add the Claude app, then Add to Slack, and approve the permissions.
steps.see: The Claude app is installed in the Slack workspace.

steps.where: Slack, any channel in that workspace
steps.do: A Slack workspace admin runs /invite @Claude, then sends @Claude connect as a new message with no other text.
steps.see: Claude replies with a message only that admin can see, containing a pairing code. The code works once and expires in 15 minutes.

steps.do: Paste the code into Paste the pairing code, then click Pair workspace.
steps.see: Connected to followed by the workspace name appears under the field.

steps.where: Claude Tag setup page, launch step
steps.do: Set a monthly spend limit, select at least one public channel and decide whether to leave Let members know they can now tag Claude switched on. Click Launch Claude Tag.
steps.see: You're set appears. Claude joins the chosen channels and answers mentions there.

steps.do: Mention @Claude and ask it to summarise what the channel decided this week and list any open questions.
steps.see: Claude replies in a thread. The reply ends with a footer naming the model and a Configure link.

undo.do: Switch off Enable Claude Tag in Slack.
undo.see: Claude stops responding in Slack, including direct messages. Nothing is deleted.

undo.do: Disconnect the workspace (or have a Slack admin uninstall the Claude app).
undo.see: Claude-side data for that workspace, including transcripts and memory, is permanently deleted. Messages Claude posted stay in Slack.

plan_needed: A paid ChatGPT plan (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu). Any Slack plan. On Business the Slack app is on by default; on Enterprise and Edu an admin must enable it. If your Slack requires admin approval for app scopes, a Slack admin may need to approve the ChatGPT app.

steps.do: Open Settings and find Slack under Apps or Plugins, depending on what your account shows.
steps.see: The Slack app or plugin page.

steps.do: Select Connect.
steps.see: You're sent to Slack to authorise.

steps.do: Choose the Slack workspace you want and approve access.
steps.see: ChatGPT connects to that one workspace. To switch workspaces later, disconnect and connect again.

steps.do: Mention Slack with @ or pick it from the + menu, then ask, for example, for a summary of a channel this week.
steps.see: ChatGPT searches channels, threads and DMs you can access. Whether it asks before taking an action depends on your app permission setting.

undo.do: Select the Slack app or plugin, then Disconnect.
undo.see: Future access stops. Past chats, saved files and memories aren't deleted automatically.

plan_needed: ChatGPT Business, Enterprise or Edu with workspace credits. A ChatGPT workspace owner or admin sets it up; a Slack owner or app manager approves the app if required. Set up separately for each Slack workspace in an Enterprise Grid.

steps.do: Select the intended ChatGPT workspace.
steps.see: The workspace's admin console.

steps.do: Open Agents, select @ChatGPT agents, select Add and choose Slack. Follow the prompts.
steps.see: You're asked to connect a Slack workspace.

steps.do: Connect the intended Slack workspace and review the requested permissions. Have the Slack workspace owner or authorised app manager complete app approval if required.
steps.see: If the ChatGPT app was already installed, you may see a warning about missing scopes that a Slack admin must approve.

steps.do: Choose the connected Slack workspace, enter a recognisable name and select Create agent.
steps.see: The @ChatGPT agent is saved with its own service account.

steps.do: To limit channels, select Selected channels only, add your test channels and select Save channel restrictions.
steps.see: Channel restrictions apply to Slack channels only. They don't restrict direct messages.

steps.do: Add @ChatGPT to the channel and mention it in a fresh thread with a short request. Test a direct message separately.
steps.see: @ChatGPT replies in the thread, visible to everyone in the channel. It doesn't respond to guests or in Slack Connect channels.

undo.where: OpenAI admin console, Agents, the agent's Overview
undo.see: Responses pause and the configuration is kept.

undo.where: OpenAI admin console, Agents, the agent's Overview
undo.do: Select Delete (or Manage agent, then Delete agent), review the confirmation and select Delete.
undo.see: The agent's configuration and service account are permanently removed. The Slack app installation stays.

plan_needed: A Gemini Enterprise subscription (Google's Slack pages cover the Standard, Plus, Pay-as-you-go and Frontline editions), a Gemini Enterprise app using Google Identity, the Project IAM Admin role on the Google Cloud project, and "Access to the Slack AI add-on" as Google lists it. Not available in the everyday Gemini app.

steps.where: Google Cloud console, APIs & Services > Credentials
steps.do: Create an OAuth client ID, choose Web application and add the redirect URI https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/slack/oauth_callback.
steps.see: A client ID and client secret.

steps.where: Gemini Enterprise, the app, Integration > Slack
steps.do: Enter your Slack workspace ID (the one starting with T), the client ID and the client secret, then click Save.
steps.see: The integration is saved. Each Gemini Enterprise app can link to one Slack workspace.

steps.where: Slack install link from the Gemini Enterprise page
steps.do: Install the app in Slack and click Allow.
steps.see: A Slack workspace owner or admin can confirm it under Manage > Installed Apps.

steps.do: Each person grants one-time access when prompted.
steps.see: People can message the app directly, or mention @Gemini Enterprise in a channel. Channel replies are shown only to the person who asked.

undo.do: The Google pages we read don't describe removing the app or the integration.

plan_needed: Any Slack plan plus a Salesforce Agentforce licence. People without a Salesforce account need a provisional Salesforce licence. Slack workspace owners or admins (or org owners or admins on Enterprise), plus a Salesforce admin. Agents must use the Agentforce Employee Agent type.

steps.do: Connect your Salesforce org to Slack and map Slack members to Salesforce accounts. On Pro or Business+ the mapping is under Admin > Workspace settings > Salesforce > Users.
steps.see: Slack members are linked to their Salesforce accounts.

steps.do: Open Agents, select the agent, click the plus button next to Connections, choose Add connection, select Slack and click Add to agent. Then Commit version and Activate.
steps.see: The agent can be installed in Slack.

steps.do: Go to Admin > Manage Agentforce, review the agent and click Install agent.
steps.see: The agent is installed for the workspace. On Enterprise, install it under Organisation settings > Salesforce > Agentforce, tick workspaces and click Add to workspaces.

steps.do: Click Tools (or More), then Agents, and pick the agent under Installed agents. On mobile, tap Agentforce.
steps.see: The member can chat with the agent. Slack says agents only use information the person can access in Slack and Salesforce.

undo.do: The Slack articles we read don't describe uninstalling an agent.

from: AI apps and agents from the Slack Marketplace
plan_needed: Any Slack plan; guests can't use AI apps. If your workspace requires app approval, an owner or admin must approve the app first.

steps.do: Click Agents & tools, then AgentExchange, and search for the app.
steps.see: The app's listing. Check what scopes it asks for before installing.

steps.do: Click Add to Slack, then Allow. If you need permission, add a message for your admin and click Submit request.
steps.see: The app is installed, or a request goes to your admin.

steps.do: Click the channel name, open the Agents & apps tab and click Add agent or app. Then mention the agent with @.
steps.see: The app can now read that channel's conversation as well as your messages with it.

undo.do: The article we read doesn't describe removing an AI app.
